news.api_permissions module

Role-based DRF permissions built on Django group permissions.

class news.api_permissions.IsReader[source]

Bases: BasePermission

Only users with the Reader role.

has_permission(request, view)[source]

Allow access only to authenticated users with the Reader role.

Parameters:

  • request (rest_framework.request.Request) – The incoming API request

  • view (rest_framework.views.APIView) – The view handling the request

Returns:

True if the user is logged in and their role is Reader, False otherwise

Return type:

bool

class news.api_permissions.RolePermission[source]

Bases: BasePermission

Authorise API requests by role.

Maps each HTTP method to the matching Django model permission (view, add, change or delete) and allows the request only if the user’s group holds that permission.

has_object_permission(request, view, obj)[source]

Check whether the user may act on one specific object.

Safe (read-only) methods are always allowed. For anything that changes data, editors may modify any object, while other users may modify only objects they authored.

Parameters:

  • request (rest_framework.request.Request) – The incoming API request

  • view (rest_framework.views.APIView) – The view handling the request

  • obj (django.db.models.Model) – The object being accessed; it must have an author_id attribute

Returns:

True if the request is read-only, the user is an editor, or the user is the object’s author; False otherwise

Return type:

bool

has_permission(request, view)[source]

Check whether the user may use this endpoint at all.

Anonymous users are always refused. For logged-in users the HTTP method is looked up in method_actions and the matching Django model permission (for example news.add_article) is required. Methods that are not in method_actions are denied.

Parameters:

  • request (rest_framework.request.Request) – The incoming API request

  • view (rest_framework.views.APIView) – The view handling the request; it must define model_name (for example "article")

Returns:

True if the user is authenticated and holds the permission for this method, False otherwise

Return type:

bool

method_actions = {'DELETE': 'delete', 'GET': 'view', 'HEAD': 'view', 'OPTIONS': 'view', 'PATCH': 'change', 'POST': 'add', 'PUT': 'change'}

get_queryset()[source]

Get the list of items for this view. This must be an iterable, and may be a queryset. Defaults to using self.queryset.

This method should always be used rather than accessing self.queryset directly, as self.queryset gets evaluated only once, and those results are cached for all subsequent requests.

You may want to override this if you need to provide different querysets depending on the incoming request.

(Eg. return a list of items that is specific to the user)

news.signals module

Signal handlers for the news app.

Keeps each user’s permission group in step with their role, and notifies subscribers (by email and by webhook) when an editor approves an article.

news.signals.create_role_groups(sender, **kwargs)[source]

Create the role groups and (re)assign their permissions.

Connected to the post_migrate signal, so the groups exist after every migrate. Permissions are replaced, not added to, so the groups always match ROLE_PERMISSIONS. Codenames that do not exist are ignored.

Parameters:

  • sender (django.apps.AppConfig) – The app config that has just been migrated

  • kwargs – Other signal arguments (not used)

Returns:

Nothing

Return type:

None

news.signals.email_subscribers(article)[source]

Send the approved article to each subscriber (one email each).

Mail errors (SMTPException or OSError) are logged and swallowed, so a mail outage never blocks the approval.

Parameters:

article (news.models.Article) – The approved article

Returns:

The number of emails sent, or 0 if there were no recipients or sending failed

Return type:

int

news.signals.get_subscriber_emails(article)[source]

Emails of readers subscribed to the article’s author or publisher.

Only users with the Reader role and a non-empty email address are included. Each address appears once, even if the reader follows both the author and the publisher.

Parameters:

article (news.models.Article) – The article being announced

Returns:

The distinct subscriber email addresses

Return type:

list

news.signals.handle_article_approval(sender, instance, raw=False, **kwargs)[source]

When an article becomes approved, notify subscribers exactly once.

Does nothing for fixture loads, unapproved articles, or articles that were already notified. Otherwise it emails the subscribers, posts to the approved-articles endpoint, and sets notified to True so later saves do not notify again.

Parameters:

  • sender (type) – The model class that sent the signal

  • instance (news.models.Article) – The article that was saved

  • raw (bool, optional) – True when the save comes from loaddata, defaults to False

  • kwargs – Other signal arguments (not used)

Returns:

Nothing

Return type:

None

news.signals.post_to_approved_api(article)[source]

POST the approved article to our own /api/approved/ endpoint.

Sends the article id, title, content, author username and publisher name (or None) as JSON to APPROVED_API_URL, authenticated with the X-Internal-Token header. The request times out after 5 seconds. Any request failure, including an HTTP error status, is logged as a warning and not raised.

Parameters:

article (news.models.Article) – The approved article

Returns:

Nothing

Return type:

None

news.signals.sync_role_group(sender, instance, raw=False, **kwargs)[source]

Keep the user’s group in step with their role.

Removes the user from every role group, then adds the group whose name matches the user’s current role. Groups that are not role groups are left alone. Skipped when fixtures are loaded.

Parameters:

  • sender (type) – The model class that sent the signal

  • instance (news.models.CustomUser) – The user that was saved

  • raw (bool, optional) – True when the save comes from loaddata, defaults to False

  • kwargs – Other signal arguments (not used)

Returns:

Nothing

Return type:

None
